title: A question to the owner stands on its own

checks.name: there is a question to judge

reasons: The question meets all six criteria; one small wording slip costs a little.
The first sentence explains the task in plain words: each row of the assistant's task list gains two details, whether the task runs by itself and what starts it.
It explains why it is asking: a full page would be about 2,930 bytes, over the project's 2,400-byte cap.
Each option says what will happen, such as two calls to read all tasks, about 40% more cost per page, or the assistant having to read a missing detail as 'manual'.
It marks a recommended option and says Smaller pages is the default if there is no answer; it is about 112 words, under the 120 limit.
Minor slip: 'calls' and 'cost to read' are not explained, and it is unclear what is being called or what the cost is measured in.
